excerpt: Compare Yas Island and Saadiyat Island investment options using official market context, unit-level costs, tenant needs and future supply.
introduction:
Yas Island and Saadiyat Island offer different Abu Dhabi residential settings. An investment decision should compare the actual property, purchase cost, expected net income, competing supply and holding period rather than treating a higher transaction total as a better return.

This guide uses Abu Dhabi Real Estate Centre (ADREC) data for the first half of 2026 as dated context. Compare the district activity alongside the price, rent and features of each property.
takeaways: ADREC's H1 2026 district sales values are market activity figures, not yields or prices for a specific home.
Compare the exact unit, tenant needs, service charges and total acquisition costs on both islands.
Verify ownership rights, project status and payment obligations with the relevant authority.

sections.heading: What do official sales figures show?
sections.body:
[ADREC's H1 2026 market report](https://adrec.gov.ae/en/news/press-29---adrec-releases-the-abu-dhabi-real-estate-market-report-for-h1-2026) reports residential sales value of AED 13.3 billion for Saadiyat Island and AED 7.3 billion for Yas Island. The chart reproduces those district values for the same period. They include a mix of residential units and transaction types and do not show average apartment prices, rental yields or a future return.

ADREC also reports that off-plan transactions represented 89% of emirate-wide residential sales value in H1 2026. That is an emirate-wide measure, not a share for either island. Compare the exact ready or off-plan property and its payment timeline.

The [Abu Dhabi area guide](/journal/abu-dhabi-real-estate-2026) provides wider context; update older market information before relying on it for a new decision.

sections.heading: Understand the settings
sections.body:
[Aldar's Yas Island page](https://www.aldar.com/properties/en/uae/yas-island) describes residential opportunities on Yas. Aldar's [2026 update on Yas and Saadiyat developments](https://www.aldar.com/en/news-and-media/aldar-sales-surpass-aed-5-billion-in-the-week-leading-to-livex-abu-dhabi) identifies different communities on the two islands. These are developer sources, so verify the exact project, phase and facilities rather than assuming every feature applies to your unit.

Visit the building or site, test the route to the destinations your intended tenant uses and check parking, condition and shared areas. If off-plan, distinguish current amenities from those planned and review the signed specification. A community name alone cannot establish a view or lease demand.

Check whether the property is ready, occupied or under construction and how that affects the first possible date of use.

sections.heading: Calculate the complete cost and income
sections.body:
Add the purchase price, buyer-paid registration, brokerage, financing costs, furnishing and initial work. Request written quotes and a service-charge statement or estimate for the actual unit. DARI's [sale registration service](https://services.dari.ae/consumer-services/registration-of-sale-and-purchase-of-land-and-real-estate/) lists its current service process and fees; confirm the allocation between parties and applicability.

Use recent signed leases for similar units and deduct vacancy, service charges, management, repairs and insurance. Divide net operating income by full acquisition cost. Keep loan payments, tax and selling costs separate.

Test a lower rent and longer vacancy. A higher selling price or attractive headline yield does not prove higher net income after costs.

sections.heading: Check supply and delivery risk
sections.body:
ADREC's H1 report identifies Yas and Saadiyat among districts contributing to projected supply through 2030. A projection is not a completed count or a guarantee that all homes will be delivered on schedule. Ask which nearby projects compete with the unit and update the information as construction progresses.

For off-plan, verify project registration, contract, payment recipient, instalments and handover provisions with ADREC and the developer. Keep enough cash to meet the schedule if delivery or your plans change.

For a ready unit, inspect the actual apartment and building and review any lease, mortgage, clearance and maintenance history. A completed project still needs unit-level due diligence.

sections.heading: Verify ownership and the exit
sections.body:
Ask ADREC or the relevant registrar to confirm the buyer's right for the exact property. The [Abu Dhabi expat buying guide](/journal/how-to-buy-property-in-abu-dhabi-as-an-expat) explains investment-area and registration checks. Review title or initial registration and the seller's authority.

Seek recent completed sales of similar homes where evidence is available and keep asking prices separate. Include selling charges and any remaining loan in eventual proceeds. A district's transaction value can reflect large or numerous sales and does not guarantee that your unit can be sold quickly.

Set a holding period and reserve appropriate to a lower rent, unexpected repair or slower sale. Do not rely on an assumed capital gain to meet an instalment.

sections.heading: Compare the likely tenant
sections.body:
Identify the tenant you intend to serve and check the actual layout, storage, parking and access to work, school or services. Request evidence of comparable signed leases with similar furnishing, view and condition. Compare advertised rents with signed leases and the income collected from similar apartments.

Consider the cost and time of managing the property and the facilities that the tenant will actually be allowed to use. If exploring short stays, verify the current licensing and building rules before relying on a holiday-rental assumption.

sections.heading: Compare payment timing and reserves
sections.body:
Place each deposit, construction instalment, handover balance and any bank repayment on a calendar. Add the expected service charges and furnishing needed before a tenant can move in. Two properties with similar total prices can require cash at very different times.

Test a delay in completion or a longer search for a tenant. A reserve should cover obligations that continue even when rent is not collected. Ask the lender and developer for written terms and verify the payment recipient independently. Do not use the district-level sales values above as a substitute for a property-specific budget.

sections.heading: Request current island options
sections.body:
Browse [Aliyas Yas Island projects](/projects?emirate=Abu%20Dhabi&area=abu-dhabi-yas-island) and [Saadiyat Island projects](/projects?emirate=Abu%20Dhabi&area=abu-dhabi-saadiyat-island). [Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget and intended use.

Ask which exact units are currently available and request their price, plan, charges and ownership documents before making a decision.
